verdict.rationale: Code is portable. GitHub sync puts app code into your own repo, `eject` downloads frontend code and backend resources, and the backend is defined in code and config files. Record data is only reachable through SDK CRUD operations, and the database lives inside the platform rather than in external persistence. The eject command also creates a new Base44 project with its own app ID rather than a standalone, self-hostable app. missing for 10: a documented bulk data export in open formats (e.g. CSV/JSON/SQL dump), evidence that exported apps can run off-platform without the Base44 backend, and independent hands-on corroboration of a full exit.
